subject: ela
intro: Seventh graders cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what an informational text says explicitly and inferences drawn from it. Strong analysis points to multiple facts, statistics, or quotations rather than relying on just one.

items.prompt:
Read.

The town's recycling rose from 20% to 65% in two years. New bins appeared on every corner, and schools added recycling lessons.

What can you infer, and what evidence supports it?

steps: I combine several details: higher rate, new bins, school lessons.
Together they show a coordinated effort worked.
So I infer the town's recycling program succeeded, supported by the rise to 65%, the new bins, and the school lessons.
solution.answer: The program succeeded; evidence: the rate rose to 65%, new bins appeared, and schools added lessons.

items.prompt: Why cite SEVERAL pieces of evidence in analysis?

steps: Multiple facts make the claim more convincing.
So several pieces build a stronger, harder-to-dispute case.
solution.answer: Several facts make the analysis more convincing.

items.prompt:
Read.

Despite record profits, the company laid off workers and cut safety spending.

What might you infer about the company's priorities?

steps: Record profits yet layoffs and safety cuts suggest money matters more than people/safety.
So the company seems to prioritize profit over its workers' well-being.
solution.answer: It prioritizes profit over workers' well-being and safety.

items.prompt:
Read.

Sales of umbrellas and raincoats spiked that week.

Infer: the weather was ____.

Strong analysis uses ____ pieces of evidence.
